In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: given n points in d-dimensional space, (a) compute a maximum volume empty axis-parallel box contained in a given axis-parallel box, and (b) compute a maximum-volume axis-parallel hypercubes contained in a given hypercube.

the following two fundamental problems: Given an axis-aligned box (or cube) R in ℝd and a finite point set in R, compute the volume of the largest empty axis-parallel box (or hypercube) contained in R.

the following problems: given n points in a d-dimensional cube R, compute the largest empty axis-parallel box contained in R; and compute the largest empty hypercube contained in a d-dimensional axis-parallel cube.

, for the problem of finding the largest empty axis-parallel box or hypercube amidst n points in ℝd, the best possible approximation ratio is $1-\Theta (\frac{d}{n} )$, and the best possible running time is $n^{1+O(\frac{1}{d})}$, where d is a constant.
, given an arbitrary axis-parallel box R in ℝ2, we can find an axis-parallel empty rectangle of maximum area in R, or an empty axis-parallel square of maximum area in a cube R in ℝ3.

for the largest empty box amidst points in ℝd, we have a (1−O(1/d))-approximation algorithm that runs in O(d⋅nlogdn) time, and a (1−1/e)-approximation algorithm in O(8edε−1d⋅nlognd) time.

we provide efficient algorithms for the largest empty axis-parallel box and cube amidst a point set, which are among the most fundamental problems in computational geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem is efficiently approximable in all dimensions d≥3.

, in contrast to the case when d is a constant, the volume of the largest empty axis-parallel box (resp., cube) contained in R can be approximated efficiently in any dimension, and the running time of our algorithms does not depend on d.
